units.en: A ⟦0⟧ leads a number of ⟦1⟧ and provides bonuses to them based on the commander's skills and traits. For a list of commanders by ⟦2⟧, see ⟦3⟧.

Divisions also have divisional commanders, or officers, assigned to them. These can be seen when viewing the details of a division, or, with ⟦0⟧, when viewing the list of officers that can be promoted to generals. They are purely flavor when playing without ⟦1⟧, but when playing with ⟦2⟧, they can gain ⟦3⟧ through earning experience with their division, and new generals are promoted from them instead of being purely randomly generated.

New generals can be recruited at a cost of 5⟦0⟧⟦1⟧ for each existing general, up to a maximum of 80⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧. New admirals can be recruited at a cost of 5 ⟦4⟧⟦5⟧ for each existing admiral, up to a maximum of 80⟦6⟧⟦7⟧. Commanders cannot normally die or be dismissed, though some country-specific events will remove particular historical commanders.
Newly recruited generals have a 95% chance to start at ⟦0⟧ 1 and a 5% chance to start at ⟦1⟧ 2.⟦2⟧ This can be increased through various bonuses, e.g., ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧ spirits.
Newly recruited admirals have a 95% chance to start at ⟦0⟧ 1 and a 5% chance to start at ⟦1⟧ 2.⟦2⟧ This can be increased through various bonuses, e.g., ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧ spirits.

With ⟦0⟧, new generals are promoted from divisional commanders instead of purely randomly generated. Doing so causes the newly promoted general's assigned division to lose ⟦1⟧ of its ⟦2⟧ and to generate a new officer to replace their old divisional commander, though the experience loss is completely negated with the ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ spirit. Divisional commanders promoted to generals will keep the experience that they earned as divisional commanders. If they have at least 400⟦5⟧ experience when they are promoted, they will also randomly get a trait like ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧, or ⟦9⟧ based on the battalions and ⟦10⟧ present in the division to which they were assigned.

Generals can command up to 24⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ effectively unless they are in "⟦2⟧" mode, during which the limit is tripled to 72⟦3⟧ divisions. Above this limit, their bonuses and XP gain are reduced proportionally. The traits of generals are oriented towards specialization in different units (e.g., tanks, foot infantry), adverse terrain/climates and tactical situations (e.g., attacking forts). Generals may be promoted to ⟦4⟧ at the cost of ⟦5⟧ and the temporary loss of one skill level.

A field marshal commands army groups, large formations composed of several armies. A field marshal initially may command up to 5⟦0⟧ armies; with the ⟦1⟧ trait, this limit can be increased to seven. Their traits give general bonuses, helping any kind of unit, such as, for example, +10% recovery rate, or increasing maximum army sizes. All armies assigned to the field marshal's army group receive these bonuses.
General's traits and the field marshal's skill levels apply to subordinate armies with a ⟦0⟧ penalty. Modifiers from ⟦1⟧, such as ⟦2⟧ or ⟦3⟧, are passed down to generals with no penalty.

They can still be used as generals, but their field marshal traits will be disabled when they are not commanding an army group. However, bonuses from field marshal traits to specialized skills, e.g., the ⟦0⟧ Attack from ⟦1⟧, still apply even when a field marshal is commanding an army instead of an army group.
Admirals can command up to 10⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧. Above this limit, their bonuses and experience gain are reduced proportionally.

⟦0⟧, or ⟦1⟧, are commanders below the level of generals who are in charge of individual divisions. Just like other commanders, they gain experience when fighting in battles, though this experience does not provide any benefits until/unless they are promoted to generals. They can accrue up to 8000⟦2⟧ experience as divisional commanders.
All divisions will always have a divisional commander assigned to them. In the base game, there is a ⟦0⟧ chance that a divisional commander will be a woman, but this can be easily changed with ⟦1⟧.
Commanders have a generic skill level and specialized skills for different aspects of warfare. Only admirals gain immediate benefits from their generic level.
The specialized skills for generals and field marshals and their effects are:
⟦0⟧, increasing soft attack and hard attack of divisions. ⟦1⟧ per level
⟦0⟧, increasing defense and breakthrough. ⟦1⟧ per level
⟦0⟧, increasing the speed and value of plan preparation. ⟦1⟧ planning speed, ⟦2⟧ max planning per level
⟦0⟧, increasing the damage done to enemy ships by your weapons. Attack: ⟦1⟧ per level
⟦0⟧, increasing ship armor and decreasing enemy damage. Defense: ⟦1⟧ per level
⟦0⟧, getting ships into and out of combat faster. Fleet speed while retreating: ⟦1⟧, Positioning: ⟦2⟧ per level

With ⟦0⟧, divisional commanders (officers) do not provide any additional benefits to their division from their skill levels, but the experience they earn as divisional commanders is kept when they are promoted to generals, and they can gain a trait when this happens if they have earned enough experience.

When leveling up, a commander gains ⟦0⟧ points in specialized skills. These points are distributed randomly, but many commanders' traits skew this distribution with a hidden in-game modifier called ⟦1⟧. The same specialized skill can be increased multiple times.

For generals and field marshals, the default weights for Attack, Defense, Logistics, and Planning are ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧, respectively.⟦4⟧ For admirals, the default weights for Attack, Defense, Maneuvering, and Coordination are ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧, and ⟦8⟧, respectively.⟦9⟧ Various ⟦10⟧, such as ⟦11⟧ or ⟦12⟧, can modify these weights, increasing the chance that certain specialized skills get increased over others.

Certain ⟦0⟧ spirits, such as ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧, provide a chance to further increase one or more specialized skills whenever a commander gains a skill level. These are on top of the 3 points that would normally be gained when leveling up. They also apply when commanders gain skill levels from ⟦3⟧, such as with ⟦4⟧ for the ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ for ⟦7⟧, or ⟦8⟧ for ⟦9⟧.

Each commander may have a number of traits, represented by medal icons. Traits are acquired when units do a certain action in combat. For example, if an army under a general manages to encircle and destroy an amount of enemy divisions, the general may acquire the ⟦0⟧ trait, which boosts reconnaissance. Experience gained towards gaining traits is decreased the more earnable traits the general already has.

Generals and field marshals have a number of abilities, represented by icons on top of ⟦0⟧. Abilities can be acquired through traits, and some can be upgraded through certain ⟦1⟧. All abilities cost ⟦2⟧ (CP) to use, with the exact amount scaling based on the number of battalions in the divisions under the commander's control.

Commanders gain experience when the units under their command engage in combat. With enough experience, they will advance a skill level. For generals the amount of experience gained in each battle per hour depends on multiple factors:

The number and size of ⟦0⟧ under the general's command: Each division counts as 10%.⟦1⟧ Small divisions (less than 8⟦2⟧ battalions and support companies) count proportionately for less, e.g. a division containing only 3 battalions would count only as 3.75%.

⟦0⟧: the side dealing more damage (HP and organization combined) in the last 24 hours gains more XP while the opposite side gets less. The bonus is reduced if the battle lasted less than 24 hours yet. The side that dealt more damage gets up to 400%[23] of normal XP when dealing up to 400%[24] as much damage as it received The side dealing less damage gets their XP gain scaled down by the average equipment ratio and average organization ratio of their divisions (including reserve), e.g. when all division are at half strength and have half of their organization, the experience is scaled to 25%. These two effects do not stack with each other, i.e. each side is only affected by one of them.
